question: Which maneuver is included among the Basic Control Skills Test exercises listed in the manual?
choice_a: An emergency lane change
choice_b: Straight line backing
choice_c: A hill start
choice_d: A K-turn
explanation: The manual lists straight line backing among the basic control skills exercises, along with offset backs, parallel parks, and the alley dock.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Test Exercises

question: What is scored as an 'encroachment' during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle
choice_b: Taking more than two minutes to complete a maneuver
choice_c: Using a turn signal incorrectly
choice_d: Braking too hard during the maneuver
explanation: The examiner scores an encroachment each time the vehicle touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

question: What is scored as a 'pull-up' during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Any time the driver stops the vehicle at all
choice_b: When the driver changes gears during the maneuver
choice_c: When the driver checks a mirror
choice_d: When a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position
explanation: A pull-up is scored when the driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

topic: Skills Test Scoring - Outside Vehicle Observations
question: What is the maximum number of times a driver may look to check the vehicle's position during most basic control skills exercises?
choice_a: Unlimited
choice_b: Zero
choice_c: Four
choice_d: Two
explanation: The maximum number of times a driver may look to check the vehicle's position is two, except for Straight Line Backing.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

topic: Skills Test Scoring - Outside Vehicle Observations
question: How many looks are allowed specifically during the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Unlimited
explanation: The Straight Line Backing exercise allows only one look, unlike the general two-look maximum for other exercises.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

topic: Skills Test Scoring - Outside Vehicle Observations
question: Before exiting the vehicle to take a 'look,' what must the driver do?
choice_a: Nothing special is required before exiting
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Remove the keys from the ignition
choice_d: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
explanation: Before exiting to take a look, the driver must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s).
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

topic: Skills Test Scoring - Outside Vehicle Observations
question: What could result in an automatic failure of the basic control skills test related to exiting the vehicle to take a look?
choice_a: Failing to safely secure the vehicle or safely exit it
choice_b: Taking longer than 30 seconds to exit
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle more than once during the entire test
choice_d: Wearing sunglasses while exiting
explanation: If the driver does not safely secure the vehicle or safely exit it, it may result in an automatic failure of the basic control skills test.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

question: Why is 'Final Position/Inside Parallel' an important scoring category?
choice_a: Because each exercise must be completed in under one minute
choice_b: Because the fuel level must not change during exercises
choice_c: Because the driver must finish each exercise exactly as the examiner instructed, or be penalized and could fail the test
choice_d: Because the vehicle must be washed after each exercise
explanation: The driver must finish each exercise exactly as the examiner instructed; failing to do so results in a penalty and could cause failure.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

question: What must a driver avoid during the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over the exercise boundaries between two rows of cones
choice_b: Backing up at all during the exercise
choice_c: Changing gears during the exercise
choice_d: Using the mirrors at any point
explanation: In Straight Line Backing, the driver must back the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing over the boundaries.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Exercises

question: In the Offset Back/Right exercise, after driving straight forward to the outer boundary, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Exit the vehicle to inspect the space first
choice_b: Back the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front of the vehicle has passed the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones
choice_c: Turn the vehicle completely around
choice_d: Pull forward through the exercise without stopping
explanation: After driving forward to the outer boundary, the driver must back the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front has passed the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Exercises

question: What is required to successfully complete a parallel parking exercise?
choice_a: Parking with at least two feet of clearance from the curb
choice_b: Using only one mirror check during the maneuver
choice_c: Getting the entire vehicle completely into the space without crossing the front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones
choice_d: Completing the maneuver in under 30 seconds
explanation: Both parallel parking exercises require getting the entire vehicle completely into the space without crossing the front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Exercises

question: In the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise, on which side is the parking space located?
choice_a: The right
choice_b: In front of the vehicle
choice_c: Directly behind the vehicle
choice_d: The left
explanation: The Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise requires parking in a space that is on the driver's left.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Exercises

question: In the Alley Dock exercise, how close must the rear of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones?
choice_a: Within ten feet
choice_b: Within one foot
choice_c: Within three feet
choice_d: Exactly touching the boundary line
explanation: The Alley Dock exercise requires bringing the rear of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Exercises

question: During the on-road driving test, what must the driver do at all times?
choice_a: Use hazard lights continuously throughout the test
choice_b: Maintain exactly the posted speed limit regardless of conditions
choice_c: Wear the safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_d: Keep both windows down for the examiner's visibility
explanation: The manual requires the driver to wear a safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws throughout the on-road test.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what may the examiner do?
choice_a: Reroute the test to a different city
choice_b: Ask the driver to simulate the traffic situation by explaining what they would be doing
choice_c: Automatically fail the driver for the missing scenario
choice_d: Skip that portion of the test with no substitute
explanation: If the route lacks a certain traffic situation, the driver may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: What is considered 'unsafe coasting' when approaching a turn?
choice_a: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_b: Coasting only while in reverse gear
choice_c: Any coasting at all, regardless of distance
choice_d: Coasting for more than one mile
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear for more than the length of the vehicle while approaching a turn.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before making a turn, where should the driver stop?
choice_a: Where the driver can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead (a safe gap)
choice_b: At least one full car length beyond the vehicle ahead
choice_c: Wherever a passenger indicates
choice_d: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
explanation: If stopping behind another vehicle, the driver should stop where the rear tires of the vehicle ahead are visible, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Turns

question: When coming to a complete stop at an intersection, what is required?
choice_a: Stopping only if a pedestrian is present
choice_b: No coasting, and maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front
choice_c: Accelerating through if traffic appears clear
choice_d: Coasting the last 20 feet to save fuel
explanation: Coming to a complete stop at an intersection requires no coasting and maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what should a driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Checking traffic in all directions
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Yielding to pedestrians in the intersection
choice_d: Decelerating before entering
explanation: A driver should not change lanes while proceeding through an intersection.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the on-road test, where should the vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane
choice_b: Straddling two lanes for visibility
choice_c: In the far left lane at all times
choice_d: In the center turn lane
explanation: During urban business driving, the vehicle should be centered in the proper (right-most) lane while keeping up with traffic flow without exceeding the speed limit.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Urban Business

question: During the lane change portion of the on-road test, what is the expected sequence of actions?
choice_a: Signal only after the lane change has begun
choice_b: Change lanes first, then check the mirrors
choice_c: Make necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe
choice_d: Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light
explanation: The driver should make necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Lane Changes

topic: Expressway and Limited Access Highway Driving
question: Once on the expressway, what must the driver maintain?
choice_a: The left-most lane exclusively
choice_b: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_c: A constant distance of exactly 100 feet from other vehicles
choice_d: Maximum speed at all times
explanation: Once on the expressway, the driver must maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, which of the following is required?
choice_a: Leave the engine running in gear
choice_b: Keep a foot on the brake pedal at all times
choice_c: Turn off the four-way flashers immediately after stopping
choice_d: Apply the parking brake and activate the four-way emergency flashers
explanation: Once stopped, the driver must activate the four-way emergency flashers and apply the parking brake.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, what should the driver NOT do before the vehicle moves?
choice_a: Check traffic from all directions
choice_b: Turn the wheel before the vehicle moves
choice_c: Release the parking brake
choice_d: Activate the left turn signal
explanation: The driver should not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves when resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should the driver reduce speed?
choice_a: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Speed reduction is not necessary for curves
choice_c: Only after exiting the curve
choice_d: While in the middle of the curve
explanation: Before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Curve

question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Keeping both hands on the wheel
choice_b: Looking both directions along the track
choice_c: Maintaining a steady speed
choice_d: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
explanation: The driver must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Railroad Crossing

question: For buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards, how far from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_b: Within 10 feet
choice_c: Exactly at the rail
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
explanation: Buses, school buses, and vehicles displaying placards must stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Railroad Crossing

question: During a student discharge, how far away from students must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: At least 3 feet
choice_c: Right at the curb, next to the students
choice_d: At least 30 feet
explanation: The school bus must come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Student Discharge

question: For manual transmissions, what is required regarding clutch usage during the on-road test?
choice_a: Ride the clutch to control speed on hills
choice_b: Always use the clutch to shift; do not ride the clutch, coast with it depressed, or 'pop' the clutch
choice_c: Never use the clutch except when starting the engine
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed to save fuel
explanation: Drivers must always use the clutch to shift and must not ride the clutch, coast with it depressed, or 'pop' the clutch.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Clutch Usage

question: What is prohibited regarding gear usage during the on-road test?
choice_a: Grinding or clashing gears
choice_b: Using the correct gear for the load
choice_c: Selecting a gear that matches engine RPM
choice_d: Shifting between straightaways
explanation: The general driving behavior category for gear usage prohibits grinding or clashing gears.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Gear Usage

question: What is expected of proper brake usage during the on-road test?
choice_a: Ride the brake continuously on downhill grades
choice_b: Apply maximum brake pressure at every stop
choice_c: Pump the brakes repeatedly for smoother stops
choice_d: Brake smoothly using steady pressure; do not ride or pump the brake, or brake harshly
explanation: Proper brake usage means braking smoothly with steady pressure and not riding, pumping, or braking harshly.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Brake Usage

question: Where should a vehicle finish a left turn on a multiple lane road, according to lane usage rules?
choice_a: In the far right lane
choice_b: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_c: In any available lane
choice_d: In the center turn lane
explanation: On a multiple lane road, the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Lane Usage

question: Where should a vehicle finish a right turn, according to lane usage rules?
choice_a: In any lane except the curb lane
choice_b: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: In the center lane
choice_d: In the left-most lane
explanation: A right turn should be finished in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Lane Usage

question: According to the steering behavior category, when may a driver's hands leave the steering wheel?
choice_a: Hands should never touch the wheel during turns
choice_b: One hand may remain off the wheel at all times
choice_c: Only briefly while shifting, after which both hands must return to the wheel
choice_d: Hands may stay off the wheel whenever traffic is light
explanation: The driver must keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and must return both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Steering

question: When should a driver check mirrors and traffic in relation to an intersection?
choice_a: Only when other vehicles are visible nearby
choice_b: Only after passing through the intersection
choice_c: Before, while in, and after the intersection
choice_d: Only if a stop is required at the intersection
explanation: The manual requires checking mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Regular Traffic Checks

question: When must turn signals be canceled?
choice_a: Never; they should stay on for the rest of the drive
choice_b: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_c: Only when the examiner reminds the driver
choice_d: After exactly 10 seconds, regardless of completion
explanation: Turn signals must be canceled upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, General Driving Behaviors - Use of Turn Signals

question: Which of the following is listed as an automatic failure on the road test?
choice_a: Driver drives 2 mph under the speed limit
choice_b: Driver fails to use the seat belt
choice_c: Driver uses a turn signal earlier than necessary
choice_d: Driver checks mirrors too frequently
explanation: Failing to use the seat belt is explicitly listed as an automatic failure on the road test.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Road Test Automatic Failures

question: Besides specific driving errors, what other situation is listed as an automatic failure on the road test?
choice_a: The driver takes a route slightly different than expected
choice_b: The driver forces the examiner to take verbal or physical control of the vehicle
choice_c: The driver adjusts the radio volume
choice_d: The driver asks the examiner a question
explanation: If the driver forces the examiner to take verbal or physical control of the vehicle, this is listed as an automatic failure.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Road Test Automatic Failures

question: Can states and jurisdictions add additional automatic failure criteria beyond those listed in the manual?
choice_a: No, only the federal government can add automatic failures
choice_b: Only Louisiana may modify the list, and only for school bus endorsements
choice_c: No, the list is fixed nationwide and cannot be changed
choice_d: Yes, states and jurisdictions may add additional automatic failures as they see fit
explanation: The manual notes that states and jurisdictions may add additional automatic failures as they see fit.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Road Test Automatic Failures

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify?
choice_a: The number of support columns
choice_b: The speed limit posted on the overpass itself
choice_c: The manufacturer of the overpass
choice_d: The posted clearance or height
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, Bridge/Overpass/Sign
